text:
maya: FYI Acme reported a structured-mode JSON parse error on our hosted API. They POST to /v1/generate with structured_output enabled and get a 400 'invalid JSON' during streaming. Repro payload they sent below.

sara: Do we have the raw payload or chunk logs?

maya: From the customer (sent as-is):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"id":"evt-123","message":"Error at C:\\services\\auth\\logger.js:45\\nTypeError: Cannot read property 'x' of undefined\\n    at Object.module.exports (C:\\services\\auth\\logger.js:45:13)\\n    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:93:5)"}'
```
They say the payload is valid JSON, but when we stream structured-output the client JSON parser errors out — seems to happen when long log lines include backslashes and the server emits a chunk that ends with a single backslash.

jon: We've seen chunk-boundary escape quirks before but this one is interesting because the field is a long single-line string (no explicit \n until escaped). If a chunk ends with a lone backslash and the next chunk starts with `n` it can turn into an escape sequence. Any internal repro yet?

liam: I repro'd locally with streaming + structured=true using repeated backslashes. Minimal repro (node):
```js
const payload = { id: 'evt', message: 'C:' + '\\\\\\\\\'.repeat(120) + 'end' };
// POST with streaming enabled
// Client JSON parser throws: SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input
```
Behavior: when the writer splits chunks mid-string, a trailing single backslash at a chunk end causes the assembled stream to become invalid JSON for some client parsers.

maya: Customer also noticed higher latency when requests routed to Dedicated — they think batching/packing changed chunk boundaries which made the issue surface more. They hit many retries and noticed a billing spike.

sara: Workarounds to suggest to Acme: pre-escape backslashes (double them) or base64-encode long log fields before sending. We'll mention cost implications. Server-side quick mitigations: sanitize/escape backslashes before streaming OR ensure we never terminate a chunk with a single backslash.

jon: I'll open an eng-runtime ticket: "streaming: backslash escape at chunk boundary corrupts JSON-mode output" and attach liam's repro and customer sample.

inc-bot: Incident created: R-2026-3105 streaming-backslash-boundary (assigned: jon)

liam: Quick triage notes: probable root cause is an assumption in the structured JSON emitter that chunk breaks are safe inside strings. Need to either emit an extra escape char when chunk ends with '\\' prefix or change chunking to be aware of escaping. Also add tests for long windows paths and sequences of backslashes / surrogate pairs.

maya: Can we give Acme an ETA? They're blocked on ingestion pipeline.

jon: Hotfix plan: patch emitter to avoid single trailing backslash at chunk end (emit one extra backslash completion or shift chunk boundary). I'll try a branch and unit tests, canary deploy if green. ETA 6-8h.

sara: :thumbsup: I'll update Acme with the temporary fixes (escape on client or base64) and log their spike to billing for manual review.

liam: Adding regression tests: Windows paths, repeated backslashes, long single-line messages, and multibyte unicode (U+2028/U+2029) which can also affect some parsers.

maya: Thanks team — I'll follow up with customer once jon posts the PR.
